subject: MAP anchoring: final-mile derisking & procurement redline coordination
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Steinberg <elaine@steinberghealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-09T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: MAP anchoring: final-mile derisking & procurement redline coordination

Elaine —

Quick note to anchor the MAP before we hit final acceptance. Two things I want to make sure are clear before our next checkpoint:

1) Procurement redlines: I attached the Procurement_Redlines.pdf with our suggested compromises on data handling and indemnity. If Steinberg has specific clauses you cannot accept, call them out line-by-line and we will escalate.

2) Acceptance window & buffering: to avoid a hard cutoff on the close date, I proposed a 10-business-day acceptance buffer in MAP_v3.xlsx (attached). That buys time for procurement without shifting product work.

Asks:
- Can procurement confirm whether legal needs a separate review cycle versus procurement signoff?
- If procurement requires >7 business days, can we formalize a 2-week MAP slip so we can notify infra and PMs?

I copied Ben and Markus since any timeline move will touch credit/finance and the final SLA. If we need an exec escalation for a credit buffer we can start that here.

Thanks — happy to jump on a short call later today.

—Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0186

Attachments: MAP_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet), Procurement_Redlines.pdf (pdf)

From: Elaine Steinberg <elaine@steinberghealth.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@steinberghealth.com, legal@steinberghealth.com
Date: 2026-11-10T10:08:00-08:00
Subject: Re: MAP anchoring: final-mile derisking & procurement redline coordination

Stephanie —

Thanks for the clear breakdown and the attachments. Quick update from our side: procurement has flagged two items that require legal review (data residency appendix and the indemnity paragraph). That review typically takes 7–10 business days but could slip to 12 if counsel requests vendor-side edits.

We are optimistic the redlines are minor, but given resource constraints on our side I need to ask for a short MAP extension to keep the project healthy and avoid a surprise go/no-go. Proposed change: shift Acceptance Target from 2026-11-30 to 2026-12-14 and add a 10 business day acceptance buffer.

On credits — procurement asked whether Redwood can offer a small goodwill credit tied to extended acceptance to offset administrative churn. They asked for a figure to take to leadership.

I appreciate you escalating if that is within your authority.

On call scheduling: I can do a 20-minute sync tomorrow morning if that helps.

—Elaine
VP of Digital Strategy | Steinberg Health
elaine@steinberghealth.com

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-10T12:45:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: MAP anchoring: final-mile derisking & procurement redline coordination — escalation request

Team —

Summary: Steinberg is asking for a 2-week shift to the acceptance target (new target 2026-12-14) while legal reviews redlines. Procurement also requested a goodwill credit to cover admin churn.

Proposal (recommended):
- Approve a one-time credit of $25,000 (applied to first invoice) conditional on signed PO by 2026-12-01.
- Formalize a MAP amendment with the Acceptance Target moved to 2026-12-14 and a 10-business-day acceptance buffer (document: MAP_v3.xlsx).
- Offer a 20-minute call with Steinberg legal to walk redlines and accelerate resolution.

Rationale: preserves product rollout cadence, keeps the commitment window predictable for our infra team, reduces escalation likelihood.

Ben — can you confirm credit approval path (finance threshold and whether you need a legal/CS signoff)? Markus — if you can draft a short amendment we can send to Elaine by COB today. I attached an Escalation_Auth_Request.docx with my write-up to support the ask.

If we do not approve the credit, procurement may insist on a hard pause which risks losing runway. I prefer the credit + amendment approach.

—Stephanie
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference

Attachments: Escalation_Auth_Request.docx (docx)

From: Elaine Steinberg <elaine@steinberghealth.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@steinberghealth.com
Date: 2026-11-12T11:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: MAP anchoring: final-mile derisking & procurement redline coordination

Stephanie / team —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the proposed approach. Steinberg accepts the MAP amendment as outlined (Acceptance Target: 2026-12-14; 10-business-day buffer). Procurement will route a PO to you by 2026-11-25 if the credit is confirmed. Our legal team will try to complete redline review within the 7–10 business-day window and will flag any material changes.

Next steps:
- Please send the MAP amendment and the short credit agreement for internal signature.
- I will aim to get the PO submitted by 11/25 assuming finance approves the $25k credit on your side.
- Let's hold a 20-minute call on 11/13 at 9:30 AM PT to walk the redlines (send invite).

Thanks — looking forward to closing this smoothly.

—Elaine
VP of Digital Strategy | Steinberg Health
